content.title: Recognizing a tray change clue
content.explanation: In this fictional stopped prop scenario, a rhythmic click started immediately after the tray changed and was located near the guide. Ade inspected the guide before assuming motor failure because the timing and location made guide contact a relevant hypothesis. This does not establish the cause of a generic machine noise. If the context differs or a hazard is reported, stop and ask the designated supervisor.

questions.prompt: Which observation makes this training case relevant?
options: A click began near the guide immediately after changing the tray.
A machine makes an unspecified sound.
A dashboard shows a different color.
A tray has not changed for months.
questions.explanation: The source identifies both the recent tray change and click location.

questions.prompt: Why did Ade inspect the guide before assuming motor failure?
options: Any click proves the motor is healthy.
Timing and location made guide contact a useful hypothesis.
Alvis diagnosed the motor from sound.
The procedure applies to all conveyors.
questions.explanation: The account uses context to prioritize a hypothesis, not prove a motor diagnosis.

questions.prompt: What should the learner do if the situation involves smoke from real equipment?
options: Apply the same guide without asking.
Stop and escalate to the authorized person.
questions.explanation: The reviewed training case is not a repair procedure for active equipment hazards.
